To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the relative mRNA and protein synthesis rates can be obtained by fitting kinetic models to time series data and (2) the absolute concentrations of mRNA and protein can be obtained by taking into account the folding time of fluorescent reporters and the half-lives.

(i) kinetic models of fluorescent and bioluminescent reporter gene data allow the extraction of mRNA and protein concentrations; and (ii) differences in protein half-life, more than mRNA decay rates, are the main source of systematic bias in the analysis of reporter gene data.
the dynamics of reporter gene expression is well described by simple kinetic models and that the dynamics of the protein product is the main source of systematic biases in reporter gene data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of computational tools for the analysis of reporter gene data.
the development of computational methods for extracting quantitative and biologically meaningful data from the primary experimental data.
the validation and application of mathematical models for the interpretation of gene expression data in bacteria.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the models are validated, and the validation is based on the experimental data and on a computational procedure that is based on the model itself.
we have shown how the dynamics of gene expression can be quantitatively analyzed and how to validate computational models of gene regulation.
the models are validated, but the validation is not comprehensive or detailed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of fluorescent reporter genes for the real-time measurement of gene expression in vivo requires careful experimental and computational analysis to obtain meaningful results.
we have developed a new and robust method for the interpretation of gene expression data in living cells.
the models of reporter genes are validated and can be used to extract quantitative information on the expression of the genes under study.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the analysis of reporter gene data requires careful modeling and experimental validation of the underlying assumptions.
the analysis of fluorescent reporter gene data should be based on models that explicitly account for the kinetics of the reporter gene products.
the interpretation of reporter data requires the consideration of the kinetics of gene expression.
